findings: The complete November and May Terminal guides document the same merchant duty to offer physical or email receipts, Stripe-triggered delivery for specified customer email on capture or via a post-checkout update, and separate EMV obligations for custom receipts.
Test-key Terminal payments do not send automatically in either capture; operators can view or manually send through the Dashboard. The mapped summary omits this important exception.

Custom receipts must include application_preferred_name and dedicated_file_name, and account_type outside the documented US exception. They can use API or SDK receipt details after confirmation, with cardholder preferred_locales only if provided.
substantive_changes: No substantive functional change between the two Terminal captures. November retargets the confirmation deep link to process=inspect; spacing, Markdown emphasis/escaping and receipt illustration destination are presentation or navigation.
historical_claims_to_preserve: The old raw header dates its capture 2025-05-01, while 2026-05-01 in the source frontmatter is the ingest date. Keep distinct capture dates for both raws.

Keep automatic capture-time email and post-checkout-trigger branches distinct, preserve test-key manual handling and optional locale availability, and maintain the client/server/JS object and US account_type qualifications.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/features/receipts, the 2026-11-07 and 2025-05-01 captures document identical behavior for source-stripe-terminal-receipts. A Terminal merchant must offer a physical or email receipt. Stripe does not automatically send test-key receipts and the Dashboard operator can view or manually send them (old raw lines 8-12 and new raw lines 9-13). With the customer's email, the integration can set receipt_email on PaymentIntent creation and Stripe sends a prebuilt compliant email at capture. After checkout, updating the PaymentIntent's receipt_email is a separately documented trigger (old raw lines 14-27 and new raw lines 15-28). For a custom emailed or printed EMV receipt, receipt data is available after confirmation. Include application_preferred_name, dedicated_file_name and account_type, with account_type optional in the US. API integrations use the Charge card-present receipt field and native clients have ReceiptDetails references; JavaScript matches the API PaymentIntent object. Card-derived preferred_locales are available if provided (old raw lines 30-55 and new raw lines 31-56). The mapped summary preserves the two approaches and most of those fields, but omits the test-key exception and the condition on preferred_locales, and compresses the two email triggers.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/features/receipts, keep source-stripe-terminal-receipts tied to the 2025-05-01 full raw and retain the full 2026-11-07 raw as reference (old raw lines 1-2 and new raw lines 1-3). The capture reproduces the same implementation. The iOS link escaping, image destination, emphasis and table layout are presentational, while the confirm-payment destination gets process=inspect as navigation (old raw lines 14-41 and new raw lines 15-42). Restore the already documented Dashboard-only test handling and optional locale availability. Keep the capture-stage and post-checkout email actions separate, and preserve the US account_type exception (old raw lines 8-12 and old raw lines 23-25 and old raw lines 38-55, new raw lines 9-13 and new raw lines 24-26 and new raw lines 39-56). Preserve reciprocal stripe-terminal, Stripe index and company routes, and route general email mechanics to source-stripe-receipts instead of the present self-link. The distinct general guide dated 2026-05-11 mentions verified testing-user exceptions (raw/stripe-receipts-2026.md:52-54), whereas the 2026-11-07 general capture also requires manual test receipts (raw/stripe-receipts-2026-11-07.md:23-27). Keep the Terminal qualification tied to the two Terminal captures rather than applying the dated general exception.
